Nevertheless, several core technical challenges remain to be urgently addressed: how to efficiently recruit endogenous MSCs to the site of damaged cartilage, how to direct the chondrogenic differentiation of the recruited MSCs, and how to preserve their stemness and proliferative capacity during inflammatory micro-environment. In this study, we aimed to achieve the direct recruitment and chondrogenic promotion of endogenous stem cells using DNA-based nanodevices, with the ultimate goal of facilitating cartilage repair. Results: We first successfully designed and synthesized triangular DNA frameworks (tDONs) via a self-assembly approach. Leveraging the editable, modifiable, and biocompatible nature of DNA nanostructures, we equally loaded or conjugated the collagen II-targeting peptide WYRGRL (WY), the MSC-targeting aptamer Apt19S, SOX9 plasmid, and resveratrol (Res) onto an integrated DNA nanodevice, designated as a DNA nanorobot (DNR). The resulting DNR was capable of selectively targeting cartilage, prolonging intra-articular residence time, and, through the cooperative action of WY and Apt19S, recruiting MSCs in situ to the affected cartilage surface. Subsequently, the recruited endogenous MSCs efficiently internalized the DNR modified with the SOX9 plasmid, which directly promoted chondrogenic differentiation. Concurrently, the loaded Res was gradually released as the DNA structure underwent disassembly, thereby enhancing the maintenance of stemness and the proliferative rate of MSCs. Overall, the constructed DNA nanorobot exerted a protective effect against chondrocyte deterioration, preserved extracellular matrix homeostasis, and mitigated cartilage degradation, with no apparent adverse effects. Conclusion: This study provides a novel strategy for OA therapy by exploiting the advantages of DNA nanodevices to efficiently recruit endogenous MSCs to cartilage defects. Through the combined actions of the loaded bioactive agents, the prepared DNA nanorobot directly induced chondrogenesis and alleviated cartilage degradation, underscoring its potential as a promising therapeutic candidate for OA.

items.title: Pleural mesothelioma cell-derived sEVs promote epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and T-cell suppression through the PD-L1 pathway
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background Pleural mesothelioma (PM) is a highly aggressive malignancy with limited durable responses to immune checkpoint blockade, largely due to poorly defined tumour-intrinsic mechanisms of immune evasion. Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) have emerged as key mediators of tumour progression, yet their role in coordinating phenotypic plasticity and suppressing anti-tumour immunity in PM remains poorly understood. Methods Given the central role of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in tumour aggressiveness, we investigated whether PM cells of the biphasic histologic subtype exploit sEVs to propagate EMT-associated and immunomodulatory signals. sEVs were isolated from human (MSTO-211H, NCI-H28) and murine (AB1, AB22) PM cell lines using differential ultracentrifugation and comprehensively characterized via nanoparticle analysis, immunoblotting, proteomics, and cytokine profiling. A 3D multicellular organoid model incorporating immune cells was used to assess sEV-mediated effects on the tumour immune microenvironment. Results Biphasic/mesenchymal PM cells and their sEVs were selectively enriched in TGF-β1 and EMT-related transcriptional regulators. Consistently, exposure of epithelial NCI-H28 and AB22 cells to sEVs from biphasic PM cells induced hallmark EMT features, including reduced EpCAM, increased vimentin expression, and enhanced migration and proliferation, as confirmed by immunofluorescence. Notably, PD-L1 was significantly elevated in biphasic cell-derived sEVs, prompting functional evaluation in a physiologically relevant 3D tumour–immune co-culture system. PD-L1–positive sEVs suppressed CD8⁺ T-cell proliferation and decreased CD8 expression, demonstrating a direct vesicle-mediated mechanism of immune suppression. Tumour microenvironment profiling of biphasic PM further revealed a stromal-rich and immune-suppressed niche consistent with these effects. These findings establish that biphasic PM-derived sEVs act as drivers of EMT and PD-L1–mediated T-cell inhibition, implicating sEV-associated signalling pathways as promising targets to overcome immunotherapy resistance in pleural mesothelioma. Conclusions Biphasic/mesenchymal PM-derived sEVs drive phenotypic transition and immune reprogramming in pleural mesothelioma. Targeting sEV-mediated intercellular communication may represent a novel strategy to enhance immunotherapy efficacy in this disease.

items.title: An AI-ready compositional framework for mechanistic aging research and in silico intervention testing
items.abstract_or_text: Aging is a network-level phenomenon, with its hallmarks interacting through dense feedback loops across vastly different timescales. Decades of reductionist research have produced thousands of mechanistic models of narrow subsystems, but no straightforward way to integrate them into one comprehensive system. Consequently, whole-cell and multi-hallmark aging models remain rare, manually constructed, and relatively small, despite broad agreement on their importance. The emergence of autonomous research agents offers a way to distribute this modeling effort across humans and artificial intelligence and thereby greatly accelerate it, but only if the underlying substrate allows agents to readily compose and analyze models with built-in validation checks and modeling guidance, without extensive custom code. We present hallsim, a JAX-native compositional simulation framework designed as the mechanistic substrate for agent-orchestrated research. It provides composability, end-to-end differentiability, GPU execution, and automated analysis and model-selection tools that facilitate composite model construction and fine tuning. The framework makes it easier to propose a mechanistic hypothesis, integrate it into an existing composite, reparametrize it against observed data, and batch-test it across different initial conditions. We demonstrate the co-simulation and in silico perturbation of three independently published kinetic models spanning genomic instability, nutrient sensing, and proteostasis. The models are connected by four edges and calibrated against a public dataset. Additionally, we train a Neural ODE surrogate and compose it alongside the mechanistic modules in a hybrid composite, demonstrating that mechanistic and neural models can function as complementary components of the same system.

items.title: Machine learning–based dynamic prediction model for postoperative malnutrition risk in esophageal cancer patients A retrospective study
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background Malnutrition is the most common postoperative complication associated with esophageal cancer (EC), which severely impacts patient survival outcomes. However, early predictive strategies for postoperative malnutrition in EC patients remain underdeveloped. Objective This study aimed to develop a dynamic predictive model for postoperative malnutrition in EC patients, to facilitate early clinical identification and timely intervention of at-risk individuals. Methods In this study, 805 EC patients were enrolled as the training and validation set. Additionally, 101 EC patients were enrolled as the external validation set. Baseline data, pathological features, and biochemical indicators were collected at 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively. LASSO regression was used to screen baseline characteristics at 1 month postoperatively. Four machine learning models (Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, Decision Tree, and Random Forest) were constructed and compared via 10-fold cross-validation to select the optimal one, which was then externally validated at 3 and 6 months. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and AUC, and SHAP was applied to interpret feature importance. Results The prediction model constructed using Random Forest demonstrated favorable predictive performance. The AUC value of the model at 1 month postoperatively was 0.974 (0.9491-1), and the AUC values with 95% confidence intervals (CI) for external validation at 3 and 6 months postoperatively were 0.814 (0.726-0.900) and 0.801 (0.714–0.889). Additionally, feature importance analysis revealed that BMI below 18.5 kg/m², weight loss > 3 kg within 3 months, and age > 70 years were associated with a higher risk of malnutrition. Conclusions This study developed a postoperative malnutrition risk prediction model for EC patients based on Random Forest, which accurately predicts malnutrition risk at 3 and 6 months postoperatively, thereby providing auxiliary decision-making support for early clinical identification.

items.title: Emotion Recognition From AI-Generated and Human Faces: Performance, Mental Health, and Demographic Diversity
items.abstract_or_text: Facial emotion-recognition tasks are widely used to investigate social-cognitive differences across mental health conditions, but theirscientific value depends on the faces used to measure performance. Established photographic databases are difficult and expensive toexpand, and many provide little ethnic diversity. AI-generated faces offer a more representative, flexible, and scalable alternative,provided they capture the same clinically relevant individual differences as photographs of human faces. We compared 161photorealistic AI-generated faces with 72 images from FACES, an established human-photograph set. Prolific participants contributed83,206 valid trials; 77,238 trials covering the six shared emotions entered the primary comparison (accuracy n = 1,047; responsetime n = 1,046). AI-diverse expressions were recognised more accurately (89.12\% vs.\ 81.72\%) and faster (2.29 vs.\ 2.64 s) thanFACES expressions, while AI-diverse and AI-White performance did not differ significantly. The AI task retained the individual differences needed for research: lower accuracy on both sources was associated most consistently with psychotic-like experiences and obsessive-compulsive symptoms, with magnitudes aligned with previous literature. AI-diverse and FACES accuracy correlated at r = .56, and corrected split-half reliability was .70 and .60, respectively. Women were more accurate than men; participant ethnicity was unrelated to performance. Higher AI accuracy indicates that the expressions were clear; it does not show general psychometric superiority, possibly because very easy items can compress differences among high performers. The combination of clear expressions, comparable symptom sensitivity, and broader representation shows that generative AI can modernise a core social-cognition research tool while making stimulus design more controllable, expandable, and shareable.

items.title: Offline Contextual Bandits for Lung Donor--Recipient Matching: A Retrospective Feasibility Study
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Lung donor--recipient matching requires balancing recipient medical urgency with expected post-transplant benefit. Conventional prediction models estimate outcomes for historical donor--recipient pairs but do not directly compare alternative candidates for the same donor. We developed an offline contextual-bandit framework to assess the feasibility of learning donor-centered lung-matching policies from historical registry data. Methods: We used linked United Network for Organ Sharing (UNOS)/Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN) Standard Transplant Analysis and Research files to identify 8,529 lung transplant allocation events from 2023 through 2025. Each event included the historical recipient and nine date-matched, ABO-compatible pseudo-candidates. The reward combined 72-hour respiratory-support-free survival (weight, 0.75) with a normalized initial Composite Allocation Score waitlist medical-urgency score (weight, 0.25). We trained a pessimistic neural lower-confidence-bound contextual-bandit policy (NeuraLCB) and evaluated it on held-out donor events using matched-action evaluation and self-normalized inverse propensity scoring (SNIPS). Results: The reconstructed dataset contained 85,290 donor--candidate rows. In the held-out set of 1,706 allocation events, the observed clinician reward was 0.534 (95\% CI, 0.518--0.549). NeuraLCB agreed with the historical recipient in 174 events (10.2\%), with a matched-action reward of 0.616. The SNIPS-estimated value of the NeuraLCB policy was 0.649 (95\% CI, 0.568--0.717), corresponding to a paired difference of +0.116 (95\% CI, +0.035 to +0.181) relative to observed clinician reward. However, the effective sample size was 51.5 events, indicating limited overlap between the learned and estimated historical policies. Conclusions: This study demonstrates the feasibility of constructing and evaluating an offline contextual-bandit framework for lung donor--recipient matching using registry data. The estimated policy value was higher than the observed historical reward, but this finding is exploratory because candidate sets were reconstructed and off-policy evaluation had limited overlap. Verified offer sets, time-stamped candidate data, explicit compatibility constraints, and prospective evaluation are required before clinical use.

items.title: Deep Learning in the Diagnosis of Choroidal Melanoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Purpose: Uveal melanoma (UM), particularly its most common subtype, choroidal melanoma (CM), is the leading intraocular malignancy in adults. Early diagnosis is crucial for improved prognosis, but accurately identifying small or early lesions remains challenging due to limitations in imaging. Artificial intelligence, especially deep learning (DL), shows promise for enhancing diagnosis and risk assessment of choroidal lesions. This study summarized DL models' diagnostic performance, clinical usefulness, limitations, pooled estimates, and research needs for detecting CM. Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted following PRISMA guidelines. Databases searched included PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and Embase up to August 3rd, 2026. Our analysis comprised research studies that used DL to diagnose CM among other conditions. Quality assessment was performed using the QUADAS-AI tool. Results: Ten studies met the inclusion criteria for the qualitative synthesis. Six of the ten studies were included in the meta-analysis. The pooled sensitivity was 0.92 (95% CI, 0.89–0.94). Individual study estimates of sensitivity ranged from 0.80 to 0.96. The pooled specificity was 0.97 (95% CI, 0.79–1.00). Across the included studies, individual specificity estimates ranged from 0.76 to 1.00. The leave-one-out sensitivity analysis showed that the pooled sensitivity and specificity estimates were consistent, regardless of which studies were excluded. Conclusion : Our study strongly supports the use of DL in diagnosing CM while highlighting areas for further research. These findings could guide future studies and clinical practices in diagnosing and managing CM.

items.title: Stepwise direct reprogramming of adult human dermal fibroblasts into tendon-like cells via transcription factor optimization and 3D culture
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Introduction : Synthetic materials are widely used in pediatric surgery for congenital diaphragmatic hernia repair when primary closure is not feasible but remain associated with complications and lack growth potential. We investigated whether direct reprogramming could promote tenogenic differentiation of adult human dermal fibroblasts (aHDFs) toward patient-derived muscle-tendon constructs for pediatric reconstruction. Methods aHDFs were transduced into directly converted tenoblasts (dTBs) using retroviral transduction of tendon-related transcription factors and Yamanaka factors. Different factor combinations and culture conditions were evaluated. Tenogenic induction was assessed using real-time RT-PCR and immunostaining for tendon markers. In vivo potential was examined by subcutaneous transplantation into NOG/SCID mice. Results Six-factor transduction induced the expression of tendon-related markers tenomodulin (TNMD) and thrombospondin-4 (THBS4), and enabled short-term engraftment in vivo . Optimization identified SCX, MKX, OCT3/4, and MYCL as a sufficient combination for tenogenic conversion. OCT3/4 promoted TNMD expression, whereas SCX affected THBS4 expression. dTBs exhibited elongated tendon-like morphology and positive TNMD and THBS4 staining. Transfer from two-dimensional to three-dimensional culture further increased tenogenic marker expression. Conclusions Direct reprogramming with SCX, MKX, MYCL, and OCT3/4 promoted tenogenic differentiation of aHDFs and induced tendon-like characteristics. This simplified strategy may facilitate development of autologous muscle-tendon constructs for regenerative reconstruction in pediatric surgery. Clinical trial registration Not applicable. This study did not involve a clinical trial

items.title: Protein language models predict artemisinin partial resistance and prioritize genetic modifiers in Plasmodium falciparum
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Artemisinin partial resistance threatens malaria control, but molecular surveillance relies largely on established K13 variants, limiting interpretation of emerging sequence variation. Here we used ESM-3 protein representations to model resistance in 1,293 Plasmodium falciparum clinical isolates. K13 sequence models generalized across temporally independent cohorts (auROC > 0.88; auPR > 0.83) and retained predictive information for geographically distinct and previously unseen K13 substitutions, correctly classifying 13 of 17 variants absent from training. Extending the framework to 167 ART-R-associated candidate genes recovered established resistance loci and provided complementary predictive information to training-selected single-variant markers. Model-based prioritization identified EXO E415G, and CRISPR–Cas9 editing showed that E415G increased ring-stage survival only in parasites carrying K13 C580Y, whereas ATP4 G1128R had no measurable effect. These findings establish protein-sequence modeling as a complementary approach for prioritizing emerging resistance-associated variation and context-dependent genetic modifiers.

items.title: Biological Assessment of Wet-Chemically Prepared SnO₂ Nanoparticles: Evaluating Antimicrobial Response and SKMEL Melanoma Cytotoxicity
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract The increasing interest on tin oxide nanoparticles due to its properties and biological activity may have promising application in the biomedical field. In the present work, SnO 2 nanoparticles (NPs) synthesized via a co-precipitation method with aqueous ammonia as precipitating agents, both with and without addition of the surfactant Triton X-100 followed by a calcination process was developed. Structural characterization, morphology, elemental composition, chemical surface nature, optical properties, and the thermal stability of SnO 2 NPs were investigated by utilizing XRD, SEM-EDS, FTIR, Raman, PL, and TGA. Antibacterial studies against six different strains were investigated by the agar well-diffusion method. The highest inhibition zone was found against Klebsiella pneumoniae (12 mm for S4), and inhibition range of Staphylococcus aureus was 9 mm for S1 and S3 respectively. In vitro cytotoxicity activity against SKMEL melanoma cells showed concentration dependent of cell mortality and S4 exhibited the higher activity with an IC 50 is 66.96 µg/mL, and followed by S3 (95.57 µg/mL). We hypothesize that surface defects may drive bioactivity and the research also suggests that the synthesis condition affect the material physico-chemical and bioactivity properties and provide the base for subsequent application of SnO 2 NPs.

items.title: Utilization of a Zirconium-Based Porous Metal-Organic Framework (PCN- 224) for Enhanced Electrochemiluminescence of Porphyrin via Suppression of Aggregation-Caused Quenching
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract To achieve highly precise measurement of alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) —a key biomarker for hepatocellular carcinoma—a novel electrochemiluminescence (ECL) immunosensor was developed. This sensor is constructed based on a synergistic "donor-acceptor" system, where Au@PCN-224 serves as the ECL signal donor and CeO 2 @PDA acts as the ECL signal quenching receptor. The superior performance of this immunosensor stems from its following design advantages:(1)PCN-224 has a well-defined structure that stops TCPP ligands from clumping together through steric hindrance. This improves charge transfer efficiency, which in turn makes the electrochemiluminescence (ECL) signal stronger.༈2༉The porosity of PCN − 224 offers high - efficiency diffusion pathways for the co - reactant, which leads to the diminishment of mass transfer resistance and the augmentation of the ECL signal generation efficiency during electrochemical excitation.༈3༉The partial spectral overlap between Au@PCN-224 (donor) and CeO 2 @PDA (acceptor) enables efficient electrochemiluminescence resonance energy transfer (ECL-RET), which in turn significantly enhances the detection sensitivity for AFP. This immunosensor exhibited excellent stability, selectivity, and reproducibility across a wide detection range of 0.0001 to 200 ng·mL − 1 for AFP. These results indicate its substantial potential for clinical AFP detection and early-stage liver cancer screening.

items.title: Human second-trimester amniotic fluid as a source of induced mesenchymal stem cells for regenerative applications
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Human fetal mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (hfMSCs) display several advantageous properties compared with their adult counterparts and human amniotic fluid stem cells (AFSCs) have been shown to improve bone extracellular matrix quality and structure. However, the clinical translation of primary hfMSCs remains limited by donor-to-donor variability, limited expansion capacity and replicative senescence, which are associated with progressive loss of tissue-repair potential. To address these limitations, we reprogrammed AFSCs to pluripotency and subsequently directed AFSC-derived hiPSCs towards the mesodermal lineage to generate induced mesenchymal stem/stromal-like cells (AF-iMSCs). AF-iMSCs retained key MSC features, including expression of canonical mesenchymal markers and trilineage differentiation potential. Comparative gene-expression analysis showed that AF-iMSCs expressed higher levels of genes associated with mesenchymal stromal identity, cell signalling, adhesion, migration, extracellular matrix remodelling and osteogenic differentiation, whereas AFSCs expressed higher levels of genes linked to proliferative and growth-factor signalling. In addition, AF-iMSCs secreted small extracellular vesicles (iEVs) that promoted fibroblast migration and supported type I collagen and elastin production in vitro, indicating functional pro-reparative activity. Together, these findings suggest that iPSC-mediated derivation of AF-iMSCs provides a scalable and reproducible strategy to overcome key limitations of primary AFSCs and support the development of cell-based and extracellular vesicle-based regenerative therapies.

items.title: Scalable Computational Phenomics of Nuclear Morphology
items.abstract_or_text: Interpretable computational pathology is constrained by a trade-off between scalable learned representations and biologically explicit phenotypes. Here we present NucXplore, a nuclear phenomics framework that converts each hematoxylin-and-eosin (H&E)-stained nucleus into 129 explicitly defined features spanning morphology, chromatin, intensity, texture, color, and spatial context. A Rust-based implementation accelerates extraction 17.6-fold over the Python reference implementation. Across three histopathology cohorts, NucXplore outperformed classical descriptors and larger deep-learning embeddings while retaining feature attribution. Applied to human skin, hierarchical multiple-instance models resolved eight cellular compartments and decoded age and sun-exposure states, revealing a largely shared aging program with age and cell-specific exposure-dependent recalibration. Conditional flow matching and neural ODE integration transformed cross-sectional phenotypes into model-implied trajectories, uncovering a midlife velocity minimum, late-life re-acceleration, and cell-specific changes in trajectory magnitude and direction. Source-free domain adaptation enabled preliminary transfer of age-associated predictions to an independent hospital cohort. NucXplore thus unifies interpretable representation, high-performance computing, and dynamical modeling for cellular phenotyping from routine histology.

items.title: A national-scale digital atlas of recorded care patterns across more than 1000 diagnostic categories using real-world health data: a retrospective observational study
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Routinely collected health data can reveal recorded care around diagnosis, but disease-specific curation does not scale across thousands of conditions. We scaled a previously developed automated framework that reduces heterogeneous clinical events into standardised, diagnosis-centred summaries of real-world care patterns. Methods In this retrospective observational study, we used EST-Health-30, a pseudonymised 30% random sample of Estonian residents with health-care records from 2012 to 2024. We constructed cohorts for ICD-10 three-character diagnostic categories using the first eligible observed diagnosis after a 3-year diagnosis-free observable lookback. For each category, we summarised recorded clinical events from a 90-day pre-index window, a 30-day post-index window, and a 365-day post-index window. An enrichment-based workflow compared earlier self-comparator periods and matched population controls, then filtered and aggregated concepts across clinical domains. Diagnosis-concept relationships were assessed by rubric-guided language-model classification, and atlas plausibility and utility by ten experts. Findings Of 1645 observed diagnostic categories, 1080 met inclusion criteria, yielding 3240 diagnosis-window summaries across 509,856 individuals. Each summary characterised diagnosis-associated events by prevalence, enrichment, timing, co-occurrence, and variation between patient groups after reducing candidate concepts by 97-98%. Among 296,303 retained diagnosis-concept pairs, the language model classified 24% as directly related, 55% as indirectly related, and 21% as noisy. Experts rated the atlas highly for generating research questions (median 6.5 of 7 [IQR 6-7]), providing information difficult to obtain conventionally (6 [5-7]), and supporting observational study design (5.5 [5-6]). Interpretation The atlas makes multidimensional diagnosis-centred patterns in longitudinal health records inspectable at population scale in order to support clinical orientation, hypothesis generation, and observational study planning. Outputs represent recorded care rather than individual patient trajectories or causal effects. Funding Estonian Research Council; European Union; Estonian Ministry of Education and Research; Innovative Medicines Initiative 2 Joint Undertaking; EFPIA.

items.title: Unmasking digital despair: A language model framework for predicting depression on social media
items.abstract_or_text: Depression is one of the most prevalent mental health disorders globally. Social media content can reflect emotional states, offering real-time signals of depressive symptoms. This study aimed to develop a deep learning model to predict depression using Twitter/X data, and to characterize potential causes of depression using a large language model (LLM). Twitter/X posts from April 20, 2023, to July 24, 2024, were obtained using the key phrase (“I” or “me”) and “diagnosed with depression”. After data cleaning and GPT-4o labelling, 2,275 depressive Twitter users, and an additional 1,661 non-depressive users from tweets using the keyword “today”, were identified. A deep learning RoBERTa model for predicting depression was built on tweets from both user groups, with an 80/20 training–testing split. GPT-4o models were subsequently employed to analyze depressive users’ posts to understand potential causes for depression. The RoBERTa model achieved strong performance in predicting depression among Twitter users from their tweets, with an accuracy of 0.822, an F1 score of 0.855, and an AUC of 0.809. Common reasons for depression identified by GPT-4o models included societal pressure, low self-esteem, cultural influences, and identity-related challenges. These findings highlight the potential of deep learning models in early screening of depression using social media data. Insights into potential reasons for depression may inform targeted prevention strategies, public health interventions, and improved mental health support for at-risk populations.

items.title: A Structure-Based Machine Learning Framework for Polymer Solar Cells: Prediction, Interpretation, and Virtual Screening
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Polymer solar cells (PSCs) have attracted extensive attention due to their lightweight, flexibility, and solution-processability. However, the performance of PSCs arises from the intricate coupling of molecular structure, energy-level alignment, charge generation, transport, recombination, and morphology, posing a significant challenge for rational materials design. With the accumulation of experimental data and advances in polymer informatics, machine learning has emerged as a powerful tool for accelerating PSC research. In this work, we construct the largest experimental database of 5,797 binary bulk-heterojunction PSC devices reported from 2010 to 2025 and develop an interpretable machine learning framework that predicts device performance directly from donor and acceptor structures. Random forest models using Morgan fingerprints achieve a strong prediction of power conversion efficiency (PCE), with R = 0.85 and RMSE = 1.94%. Statistical and Shockley-Queisser limit analyses show that historical PCE improvements have been driven primarily by short-circuit current density, whereas further gains increasingly depend on open-circuit voltage. Fragment-level SHapley Additive exPlanations reveal distinct structural roles: Y6-derived acceptors with ADA’DA architectures and INCN-type end groups contribute strongly to PCE and photocurrent, while donor fragments mainly regulate voltage. Screening more than 2.2 million virtual donor and acceptor combinations further indicates that high-performance systems occupy a restricted chemical space dominated by optimized Y6-derived acceptors paired with halogenated benzodithiophene-based donors. These results demonstrate how experimentally grounded, interpretable machine learning can clarify structure-performance relationships and guide the rational design and screening of organic photovoltaic materials.

items.title: Biological treatments with Bacillus and Trichoderma reduce cassava root rot under controlled conditions
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Cassava root rot diseases, caused by diverse soilborne fungi, significantly impair crop establishment and yield, challenging effective disease management. Biological control using native microbial antagonists offers a sustainable alternative but requires evaluation against multiple pathogens and cassava genotypes. Here we screened ten Bacillus and three Trichoderma isolates in vitro against fungi associated with dry and black root rots, identifying isolates with pathogen-specific antagonistic activity. Selected agents, including Bacillus mix 3 and Trichoderma asperellum TRI81, were evaluated in planta on two cassava cultivars, demonstrating improved germination, vigor, biomass, and reduced internal colonization under controlled conditions. Bacillus mix 3 and its sequential combination with TRI81 showed the most consistent benefits, particularly in cultivar BRS Formosa. These findings support the potential of native Bacillus and Trichoderma isolates as components of integrated cassava root rot management, while emphasizing the need for further validation under natural soil and field conditions.

items.title: Synthesis, Characterisation and Biological Evaluation of Some 5- Trifluoromethylisoxazole Derivatives
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract A series of 4-(aryldiazenyl)-5-trifluoromethyl substituted isoxazole derivatives ( 3a-n and 3aa-an ) was synthesized to explore their biological potential. All compounds were characterized by analyzing their FT-IR, ¹H/¹³C/¹⁹F NMR spectroscopic, and mass spectrometric data. The DFT calculations further supported the structural assignment of the hydrazono form ( 3 ), among the possible tautomeric structures. The results of in vitro antimicrobial evaluation revealed that among all, seven candidates have shown good potential out of which compound 3ak emerged as the most potent antimicrobial agent, exhibiting remarkable antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus ( S. aureus ) and Bacillus subtilis ( B. subtilis ) with MIC value of 80 µg/mL, comparable to Ciprofloxacin (MIC = 62.5 µg/mL); and significantly higher antifungal potential against Candida albicans ( C. albicans ) with MIC value of 320 µg/mL than Amphotericin B (MIC = 1280 µg/ mL). Antioxidant screening revealed that 3j , 3l , 3aa , 3ae , 3ah – ak and 3al – an displayed strong antioxidant potential with EC₅₀ values of 62.5–125 µg/mL, in comparison to ascorbic acid (EC₅₀ = 132.7 µg/mL). In addition, 3g , 3n , 3f , 3m , 3af , 3ag , 3am , and 3an displayed excellent and 3b , 3e , 3aa , 3ae , and 3h demonstrated significant DNA protective effects against UV-induced damage at 60 µg/mL concentration. Hence, the results of the present study demonstrated that the synthesized 5-trifluoromethyl substituted isoxazoles have significant antioxidant potential along with good DNA protective potential.

items.title: Clinical Spectrum, Radiological Aggressiveness, and Diagnostic Pitfalls of Intraparenchymal Malignant Peripheral Nerve Sheath Tumor: An Institutional Case Series and Integrated Analysis of 33 Cases
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background and Purpose Intraparenchymal malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor (MPNST), also referred to as malignant schwannoma, is an exceptionally rare and highly aggressive malignant tumor. Its nonspecific clinical presentation and heterogeneous radiological appearance frequently lead to preoperative misdiagnosis. Current evidence is largely derived from isolated case reports and small case series. This study aimed to define the clinical spectrum, radiological aggressiveness, pathological features, and diagnostic pitfalls of intraparenchymal MPNST through an institutional case series and an integrated analysis of published cases. Materials and Methods We retrospectively reviewed three pathologically confirmed i ntraparenchymal MPNST cases treated at our institution and systematically reviewed previously published intraparenchymal MPNST cases. Individual patient-level data were extracted, including demographic characteristics, clinical presentation, tumor location, preoperative diagnosis, radiological features, histopathological and immunohistochemical findings, treatment strategy, recurrence, dissemination, and survival outcome. Imaging features and outcome variables were defined using standardized criteria, and descriptive statistics were applied. Results A total of 33 patients were included, comprising three institutional cases and 30 published cases. Adolescents and young to middle-aged adults predominated, and males were slightly more common than females. Tumors most frequently involved the supratentorial lobes, particularly the frontal and temporal lobes, with some cases showing multilobar infiltrative growth. Radiologically, these tumors were usually solid or mixed solid-cystic heterogeneous masses with heterogeneous enhancement, necrosis or cystic change, peritumoral edema, ill-defined margins, diffusion restriction, bone destruction, or neurovascular involvement. Histologically, the tumors showed malignant spindle-cell morphology with variable immunophenotypic heterogeneity. S100 and/or SOX10 expression supported nerve sheath differentiation, Ki-67 indices were often elevated, and H3K27me3 loss was observed in a subset of cases. Gross total resection was achieved in 42.4% of cases, recurrence occurred in 48.5%, and the overall prognosis was dismal. Conclusion Intraparenchymal MPNST is a rare malignant tumor with nonspecific symptoms, heterogeneous imaging features, complex pathological profiles, and high recurrence risk. Lobar intraparenchymal involvement may represent an underrecognized phenotype and can mimic glioma, metastasis, or inflammatory lesions. Recognition should rely on a pattern-based assessment integrating clinical background, radiological aggressiveness, pathological immunophenotype, and treatment risk. Maximal safe resection combined with adjuvant therapy and long-term surveillance remains central to management.

items.title: Empirical antibacterial use, escalation, microbiological profile, and outcomes in febrile neutropenia: An ambispective observational study
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Febrile neutropenia requires rapid empirical antibiotic therapy, with regimen selection shaped by local prescribing practice and pathogen patterns. We described starting treatment, later drug changes, microbiological findings, and inpatient outcomes. Methods: This ambispective cohort comprised 96 episodes from 90 patients admitted to a tertiary-level teaching hospital. Treatment and outcome analyses used each episode as the unit of observation. Recorded variables included the starting antibiotics, later regimen modification, microbiology, hospitalization length, invasive fungal infection (IFI) as captured in study records, and disposition. Comparisons based on escalation status were exploratory. Results: Cefoperazone-sulbactam appeared in 62/96 initial regimens (64.6%), amikacin in 42 (43.8%), teicoplanin in 28 (29.2%), and meropenem in 14 (14.6%). Eighteen episodes (18.8%) required a change that broadened or substituted antibacterial therapy. Among 31 microbiologically documented infections, 22 (71.0%) yielded Gram-negative organisms and 9 (29.0%) were polymicrobial. Median length of admission was 18.5 days in the escalation group and 9 days in the remainder (p Conclusion: Antibacterial management differed within this cohort, with treatment escalation required in 18 of 96 episodes. Gram-negative organisms comprised most microbiologically confirmed infections. Escalation marked a clinically complex course with prolonged hospitalization and greater observed mortality; the observational design does not establish comparative efficacy or causation. Keywords: Chemotherapy-Induced Febrile Neutropenia; Anti-Bacterial Agents; Drug Prescriptions; Drug Resistance, Bacterial; Treatment Outcome

items.title: CREB3L1 regulates mitochondrial bioenergetics and cytoskeletal remodeling during axon specification in developing neurons
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract The transition from a neural progenitor to a mature, polarized neuron requires a substantial and strictly coordinated investment of cellular energy. While the genetic cascades governing cytoskeletal remodeling and structural polarity are well documented, how these programs are metabolically supported during early differentiation remains a fundamental question in neurobiology. In this study, using three different species as study models: rats, mice, and humans and an unbiased transcriptomic approach, we identify the transcription factor CREB3L1 as a key molecular regulator that dynamically modulates both neuronal morphogenesis and cellular bioenergetics. Through targeted CRISPR-Cas9 knockout in human iPSC-derived glutamatergic neurons and functional silencing in rodent models, we demonstrate that the loss of CREB3L1 disrupts critical cytoskeletal networks required for axonogenesis. This structural collapse is accompanied by a bioenergetic paradox: CREB3L1-deficient neurons trigger a compensatory upregulation of mitochondrial biogenesis programs; however, these upregulated networks are functionally defective, exhibiting dissipation of membrane potential and impaired metabolic capacity. In vivo assays using in utero electroporation reveal that this bioenergetic failure delay developing neurons in a multipolar state, thereby impairing the multipolar-to-bipolar transition relevant for proper cortical integration. Collectively, our findings define CREB3L1 as a transcriptional regulator controlling both structural architecture and mitochondrial homeostasis, offering a novel, cross-species framework for understanding neurodevelopmental vulnerabilities and neuropathologies.
